wants.topic: Gulf region power‑plays and underworld stories (e.g., Dubai’s criminal networks, Qatar’s birth)
wants.evidence: World Files video “ദുബായ് അധോലോകത്തിന്റെ ഞെട്ടിക്കുന്ന കഥ | Super Cartel” (vsNormal 18.7) and “How Qatar Was Born Part 2” (vsNormal 4.87) with comments praising the shocking details and asking for more similar tales

wants.topic: Hot‑button current geopolitics with a partisan edge (EU‑Poland clash, migrant riots in Germany, Iran‑Israel tensions)
wants.evidence: Tousi TV “BREAKING: EU Globalists Launch Coup In Poland” (vsNormal 4.43) and “BREAKING: Europe At WAR – Migrant Riots Reach Germany” (vsNormal 3.89); comments show high engagement (hundreds of likes, calls to action)

wants.topic: Deep‑dive ancient empire narratives that are less covered in mainstream US media (Mughal Empire, Indus Valley, Ottoman rise)
wants.evidence: The Time Page “The Rise and Fall of the Mughal Empire” (vsNormal 8.83) despite zero subscriber base; viewers comment “more detailed content like this”

wants.topic: Mystery/obscure historical sites and events (e.g., Velliyamkallu Sacrifice Rock, regional folklore)
wants.evidence: World Files “Mystery of Sacrifice Rock” (vsNormal 2.55) with comments lauding the thorough presentation and asking for similar hidden‑history videos

wants.topic: Series/part‑2 formats that continue a story line
wants.evidence: World Files “How Qatar Was Born Part 2” (vsNormal 4.87) and multiple comments requesting “part 3” or “continue the story”

gaps: Balanced, fact‑checked coverage of controversial geopolitics (many comments demand less bias and more sources)
US‑centric historical and geopolitical analysis (the audience is US‑based but few videos focus on American history or its role in world events)
Coverage of African, Latin American, and South‑Asian contemporary history (viewers repeatedly ask “what about Africa?” or “why don’t you cover Brazil?”)
Post‑event analysis – viewers want “what happened next?” after a major event is explained
saturated: General “Rise and Fall of the Roman Empire” style videos
Broad “Mughal Empire” overviews without a fresh angle
Generic “Complete History Explained” titles without a hook
title_patterns: How X Was Born / How X Came To Power
